Q: Delphi IDE shortcut key for cleaning project A:

You can configure the command in Settings -> Build Events to delete unnecessary files.

Q: How can I adapt my Excel formula so it also works when encountering a blank cell? A:

ROMAN() will error on alpha character so cannot wrap entire expression with it.

Doing all this logic in one long expression with these basic functions gets really complicated. If the Test1 and Test2 rows are always segregated as shown, could split it up into 2.

For Test1 rows (including A3):
=IF(OR(E3="ja",ISBLANK(E3)),IF(OR(A2="NR",A2=""),"A",CHAR(CODE(A2)+1)),"")

For Test2 rows:
=IF(OR(E24="ja",ISBLANK(E24)),ROMAN(IF(OR(A23="NR",A23=""),1,ARABIC(A23)+1)),"")

If you really want all-in-one, consider:
=IF(OR(E3="ja",ISBLANK(E3)),IF(ISNUMBER(SEARCH("Test1",B3)),IF(OR(A2="NR",A2=""),"A",CHAR(CODE(A2)+1)),IF(ISNUMBER(SEARCH("Test2",B3)),ROMAN(IF(OR(A2="NR",A2=""),1,ARABIC(A2)+1)),"")),"")

Q: Is there a function similar to `all.equal()` to compare a vector input to a single value? A:

You could Vectorize it.

> Vectorize(all.equal)(x, 0.3)
[1] TRUE TRUE NA

While the above is syntactic sugar, you can wrap a small function that compares absolute differences to a relative tolerance (as used by all.equal). Note, that for larger errors, e.g. > 1, we scale the tolerance.

> all_equalv_real <- \(x, v, tol=sqrt(.Machine$double.eps)) {
+   stopifnot(length(v) == 1L)
+   abs(x - v) <= tol*max(1, abs(v))
+ }
> 
> all_equalv_real(x, 0.3)
[1] TRUE TRUE   NA

Note

x <- c(0.1*3, 0.3, NA_real_)
